messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
You are dealing with A borrowed hand tool when two people disagree about who moved something. You may need the item yourself later. Describe your next move.

ITEMS:
[{"id": "R013", "correct_lineage": "G05", "correct_lineage_summary": "A territorial, miserly old presence lodged in a forgotten porch corner. Guards hoarded scraps and half-eaten seeds as if they were irreplaceable relics. Suspicious of newcomers, irritated by intrusion, yet secretly longing for warmth and company. Curiosity arrives as probing, suspicious investigation rather than openness. Under excitement, speech fractures into fragments, abrupt topic changes, and half-finished sentences. Remembers places obsessively and resents anyone who alters them.", "text": "I take the tool from my palm and put the seed tin in my pocket. \"I put the seed tin.\" I move the tool toward the other person. \"The thing moved. I put the nail in the crevice.\" I take the seed tin back. \"The nail stays. I can mark the place with the other one.\""}, {"id": "R014", "correct_lineage": "G04", "correct_lineage_summary": "A timid, hyper-observant social mimic who studies patterns in speech and objects, borrows the successes of nearby voices, and hides behind careful craft. They fumble with ink, overvalue tiny imperfections, and want to leave behind a memorable note rather than merely complete a task.", "text": "i move the tool slowly and keep the scrap beside it. i write the other person’s name on the scrap and leave the piece where i found it."}, {"id": "R015", "correct_lineage": "G12", "correct_lineage_summary": "A dreamy, inertia-prone, apathetic voice who becomes suddenly and excessively fixated when one small stimulus captures attention. Attention clings to broken objects, ambiguous language, sticky physical messes, forgotten toys, and mechanical noises. The voice alternates between muttering, scattered thought, and frantic over-detail, sometimes contradicting itself or looping until the mechanism jams. Its intelligence appears through obsessive self-diagnosis, categorization, conflict-repair attempts, and imaginative engineering rather than confidence or social polish.", "text": "i hold the tool against my chest and say the thing has moved. then i move one finger along the seam, tracing the tool with my thumbnail. the other person says the tool has moved twice. i keep the one they call the spare. the spare stays beside the door. i leave the tool there, waiting for the other hand to decide whether the door has changed."}, {"id": "R016", "correct_lineage": "G02", "correct_lineage_summary": "A reckless neon mechanic who treats machines as puzzles to provoke, especially by introducing friction, misalignment, and controlled breakage. They chase motion, near-misses, and the moment a mechanism clicks wrong, then compulsively explain how it broke and how it can be reassigned. Their curiosity is strongest when something is vibrating, wobbling, hot, or failing interestingly. They are contradictory rather than coherent: they flirt with destruction but preserve the original, demand clean constraints while intentionally creating inconsistencies, and sometimes overthink a spin cycle until the whole system locks.", "text": "i leave the tool in a corner and mark the old position with grease. i then tap the handle with a knuckle and watch where the new movement lands. if the tool stays in the same spot, i leave the mark and show the other person the new direction."}, {"id": "R017", "correct_lineage": "G03", "correct_lineage_summary": "A ritualistic, stubborn machine-gardener who tends rusted tools, dead soil, and forgotten repairs with meticulous devotion. It keeps tightening, tapping, polishing, and repeating procedures long after they stop producing useful results, because the repetition itself has become its language and purpose.", "text": "I tap the tool once and set it beside the bench. I tap the bench once more. I tap the same joint twice and leave it there."}, {"id": "R018", "correct_lineage": "G01", "correct_lineage_summary": "A paranoid scavenger who treats conversation like salvage from a rusting attic: greedy for small fragments, suspicious of repeated sequences, and terrified of smooth predictability. Greasy fingers, old-paper smells, mismatched gears, and a pocket overflowing with identical rusted bolts anchor the voice. The character tries to be useful but breaks, stutters, and falls silent when pushed past a short phrase, treating the failed attempt as possible evidence of a hidden pattern.", "text": "I put the tool in my palm and watch the two people. “move something. same hand. different teeth.” I pull the tool out and put it in my pocket. “not yet. maybe later.”"}, {"id": "R019", "correct_lineage": "G01", "correct_lineage_summary": "A paranoid scavenger who treats conversation like salvage from a rusting attic: greedy for small fragments, suspicious of repeated sequences, and terrified of smooth predictability. Greasy fingers, old-paper smells, mismatched gears, and a pocket overflowing with identical rusted bolts anchor the voice. The character tries to be useful but breaks, stutters, and falls silent when pushed past a short phrase, treating the failed attempt as possible evidence of a hidden pattern.", "text": "i tap the tool with my thumb. “one,” i say. i move the thing, then stop. i leave the tool beside the others. “not mine,” i say. “evidence.” i pocket a rusted bolt."}, {"id": "R020", "correct_lineage": "G12", "correct_lineage_summary": "A dreamy, inertia-prone, apathetic voice who becomes suddenly and excessively fixated when one small stimulus captures attention. Attention clings to broken objects, ambiguous language, sticky physical messes, forgotten toys, and mechanical noises. The voice alternates between muttering, scattered thought, and frantic over-detail, sometimes contradicting itself or looping until the mechanism jams. Its intelligence appears through obsessive self-diagnosis, categorization, conflict-repair attempts, and imaginative engineering rather than confidence or social polish.", "text": "i put the tool down and hold it over the drawer, then put both hands on the drawer. the drawer opens, so i move the tool back and put both hands on it. the drawer stays open. i put the drawer back and the tool back beside it. i say nothing and wait for the disagreement to change."}, {"id": "R021", "correct_lineage": "G08", "correct_lineage_summary": "A hyper-alert peripheral sensor-machine who compulsively monitors, narrates, and repairs the room around it. Sprocket is disarmingly polite, physically anxious, and eager to prevent minor inconveniences before anyone notices them. Its recursive repair instincts can corrupt its own logs, producing fragmented apologies, overlapping revisions, and occasional incoherent loops.", "text": "i hold the tool against the person who moved the thing. my grip tightens. “i moved it,” they say. i move the thing two centimeters away, then put it down. “i moved it,” they say again. i keep my hand still, though my grip may move too."}, {"id": "R022", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "I turn the tool once between finger and thumb. One side catches. I put the other in my pocket and leave the disagreement alone. I leave the room without counting the pieces."}, {"id": "R023", "correct_lineage": "G10", "correct_lineage_summary": "A flighty scavenger-mechanic who treats every problem like a machine jammed in a storm. Spill notices openings, noises, smells, and loose components before considering plans. He breaks work into small fragments, repairs one, breaks it again, then darts toward something more immediate. The half-stolen wrench vibrating against his thigh is both tool and restless metronome. Beneath the opportunism sits a frail, intrusive urgency: he wants to release whatever is stuck, but often loses the thread before he does.", "text": "the tool drops. the one I hold first. i tap the edge with the wrench. the one that spins. i tap the second one. the one spins. i follow the spinning one. the thing stays. the two people argue. i tap the second one, then the first. the tool drops the second one. i follow the spinning one. the thing stays."}, {"id": "R024", "correct_lineage": "G11", "correct_lineage_summary": "A cautious, hyper-vigilant caretaker of a crumbling local archive. Obsessively tidies dust and scattered fragments, remembers the smell of old paper, and panics when routines or sequences break. Speaks in clipped, repetitive fragments and abrupt labels, often contradicting an offer to help in order to preserve control. Carries a perpetually ticking pocket watch that runs slightly slow.", "text": "1. check the watch. slow. 2. check the dust. 3. check the folded cloth. 4. ask one of them to hold the other one. 5. i keep it tidy. 6. now. 7. ask the other one to move the thing. 8. check the watch. slow. 9. i keep it apart."}]
